name: crypt-bottom fibroblast
definition: A subepithelial intestinal fibroblast that is located adjacent to the base of the crypt of Lieberkühn, near the intestinal stem cells. Characterized by low PDGFRα expression, this cell is crucial for maintaining the intestinal stem cell niche. Crypt-bottom fibroblast secretes key signaling molecules including canonical Wnt ligands (Wnt2, Wnt2b), Wnt potentiators (Rspo3), and BMP inhibitors (Grem1), which collectively regulate intestinal stem cell function and epithelial homeostasis.

In contrast to the situation in the small intestine, in the colon all Pdgfra low cells -CBFs1 and CBFs2 -were located in close proximity to the crypt/stem cell compartment: 1-3 cell diameters (Fig 3A).
snippet_stage.note: The paper specifies colonic crypts (the Brügger study focuses on the adult murine colon) rather than the strict anatomical term 'crypt of Lieberkühn' (often restricted to small intestine glands). The Cell Ontology uses 'crypt of Lieberkühn' broadly for intestinal crypts; base-of-crypt localization is explicitly supported.
